Moment China's President Xi bursts into laughter as Trump shows him mocking 'autopen' portrait of Biden

In a video posted by the White House, Trump was seen walking Xi through the portraits. After pointing at himself, he says to Xi: 'And this is the autopen... it's Biden.'

Actual Article Body:
By PERKIN AMALARAJ, FOREIGN NEWS REPORTER

Published:  18:03 AEST, 25 September 2026   |  Updated:  20:00 AEST, 25 September 2026

55

View  comments

Chinese president Xi Jinping burst into laughter after Donald Trump showed him a mocking 'portrait' of Joe Biden.

President Xi landed in Washington DC on Thursday for talks between the two superpowers.

Trump hailed his 'great friendship' with Xi and pulled out all the stops to woo the Chinese leader, greeting him on the runway on his arrival, offering him a rare tour of the presidential helicopter, and giving him a bald eagle statue.

He also took the Chinese leader to the Presidential Walk of Fame, a gallery of presidential portraits of almost all former US presidents.

The one notable exception is Joe Biden, who Trump replaced with a photograph of an autopen – a reference to Biden's use of the technology to sign legislation.

In a video posted by the White House, Trump was seen walking Xi through the portraits.

After pointing at himself, he says to Xi: 'And this is the autopen... it's Biden.'

Xi let out a hearty laugh as one of his aides appeared to translate Trump's sentence into Mandarin.

In a video posted by the White House, Trump was seen walking Xi through the portraits

Chinese First Lady Peng Liyuan, Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and US First Lady Melania Trump pose on the North Portico ahead of a state dinner at the White House in Washington, DC, USA, September 24 2026

The autopen was a hot-button issue towards the end of Biden's presidency.

The autopen is a device used to replicate a person's signature with precision, typically for high-volume or ceremonial documents. It has been employed by presidents of both major parties to sign letters and proclamations.

Trump and his supporters have made a variety of unfounded claims that Biden's use of the device while president invalidated his actions or suggested that he was not fully aware of these actions. Trump, known for his provocative style and dislike for his political opponents, repeatedly targeted Biden's use of the autopen to sign official documents during his presidency.

Before he left office in January 2025, the Democrat president used the technology to issue several pardons, including for family members, who he wanted to protect from politically motivated investigations.

Biden also commuted criminal sentences, including for non-violent drug offenders.

Trump took umbrage with this, announcing in December 2025 that he was terminating all documents, including pardons, that he said his predecessor signed using an autopen.

He wrote at the time: 'Any and all Documents, Proclamations, Executive Orders, Memorandums, or Contracts, signed by Order of the now infamous and unauthorized ''AUTOPEN',' within the Administration of Joseph R. Biden Jr., are hereby null, void, and of no further force or effect.'

'Anyone receiving 'Pardons,' 'Commutations', or any other Legal Document so signed, please be advised that said Document has been fully and completely terminated, and is of no Legal effect,' Trump wrote on Truth Social.

It comes as US and Chinese officials sit down for significant talks, which so far seem to have resulted in few diplomatic breakthroughs.

Those meetings yielded 'many new consensuses', according to Xi – but the only concrete deals announced were a promise to invite 100,000 young Americans to China for exchanges, and lending two pandas to a zoo in Atlanta.
